questions.question: Distinguish between formal and informal businesses and give two examples of each.
questions.expected_answer: Formal: officially registered (CIPC, SARS), pays tax, follows labour and business laws, keeps records, e.g. supermarket chain, bank, registered salon, mine. Informal: not officially registered, operates outside most formal systems, often cash-based, e.g. street vendor, home hair salon, informal car wash, many spaza shops.

questions.question: Give two advantages and two disadvantages of an informal business.
questions.expected_answer: Advantages (any two): easy to start; little capital; no paperwork; flexible location and hours; close to customers. Disadvantages (any two): low, uncertain income; hard to get loans; cannot bid for big contracts; no UIF/labour protection; harassment or eviction; vulnerable to crime and weather; few records.

questions.question: Explain how needs and wants create business opportunities and describe two ways to test an idea.
questions.expected_answer: Customers pay for goods and services that satisfy needs or wants, so unmet or poorly met needs and wants are business opportunities. Testing (any two): ask potential customers if and at what price they would buy; check competitors and their prices; work out costs; start small and gather feedback.
